name: Gestational Choriocarcinoma

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in Asian and African populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: FIGO Diagnostic Criteria for Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia

criteria.description: Persistently elevated or rising serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels after pregnancy
Histopathological confirmation of malignant trophoblastic proliferation without villous structures
Evidence of metastatic lesions on imaging, commonly in lungs or brain

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus elevated β-hCG levels; imaging to assess metastases supports staging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often follows molar pregnancy, abortion, or term pregnancy; β-hCG monitoring is critical

searchTerms: high pregnancy hormone levels in blood

laboratory: Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
Thyroid function abnormalities (hyperthyroidism) secondary to β-hCG
imaging: Ultrasound showing heterogeneous uterine mass without fetal parts
Chest X-ray or CT revealing multiple pulmonary nodules
Brain MRI or CT demonstrating metastatic lesions
genetic: No specific germline mutations; tumor arises from trophoblastic tissue of gestational origin
other: Histopathology showing biphasic proliferation of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without chorionic villi

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of chorionic villi on histopathology
Usually confined to uterus without metastases
Originates from germ cells rather than gestational tissue
May occur in males or females outside pregnancy context

redFlags: Rapidly rising or persistently elevated β-hCG after pregnancy
Neurological symptoms such as headache or seizures suggesting brain metastases
references: Seckl MJ, Sebire NJ, Berkowitz RS. Gestational trophoblastic disease: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Ann Oncol. 2013 Jul;24 Suppl 6:vi39-50.
Goldstein DP, Berkowitz RS. Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: 2021 update. Gynecol Oncol. 2021 Mar;160(3):661-668.
